source.label: thm:LB-main
source.quote: Consider the stochastic \problem\ with $k$ agents. Let \A\ be an exploration-separated deterministic allocation rule. Then its regret is $R(T;\, \Vmax) = \Omega(\Vmax\, k^{1/3}\, T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: Also stated as Theorem 1.6 in the introduction (with v_max normalized). Applies to truthful mechanisms for two agents (non-degenerate, scale-free) and k agents under IIA via characterization.

symbols.delta_gap: relative gap: mu_1 v_1 - mu_2 v_2 = delta * max_i v_i
symbols.gamma: exponent of the assumed worst-case regret bound O(v_max T^gamma), gamma<1

conditions: allocation rule is deterministic and exploration-separated
worst-case regret R(T; v_max) = O(v_max T^gamma) for some gamma < 1

source.label: thm:LB-delta
source.quote: In the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:LB-main}, fix $k$ and $\Vmax$ and assume that $R(T;\, \Vmax) =O(\Vmax\, T^\gamma)$ for some $\gamma<1$. Then for every fixed $\delta\leq \tfrac14$ and $\lambda < 2(1-\gamma)$ we have $R_\delta(T;\, \Vmax) = \Omega(\delta\,\Vmax\,T^\lambda)$.

results.notes: Worst-case over delta-gap instances (gap-restricted class), classified worst_case. Theorem 1.6 states equivalent version with exponent 2(1-gamma)-eps.

conditions: allocation rule deterministic, non-degenerate, satisfies IIA

source.label: thm:LB-non-scalefree
source.quote: Consider the stochastic \problem\ with $k$ agents. Let $(\A,\mathcal{P})$ be a normalized truthful mechanism such that $\A$ is a non-degenerate deterministic allocation rule. Suppose $\A$ satisfies IIA. Then its regret is $R(T;\, \Vmax) = \Omega(\Vmax\, T^{2/3})$ for any sufficiently large $\Vmax$.

conditions: allocation rule is a distribution over exploration-separated deterministic allocation rules (universally truthful randomized mechanisms)

source.quote: Consider the \problem. Let $\RandAlloc$ be a distribution over exploration-separated deterministic allocation rules. Then $$ \E_{\A\in \RandAlloc}\, \left[ R_{\A}(T;\Vmax) \right] = \Omega(\Vmax\, k^{1/3}\, T^{2/3}).$$

results.notes: Stochastic setting implied by the proof (extends Theorem 4.1 instances).

tuning: exploration length per agent T_0 = k^{-2/3} T^{2/3} (log T)^{1/3}

source.label: thm:naive-k
source.quote: Consider the stochastic \problem\ with $k$ agents. The naive mechanism is normalized,  truthful and has worst-case regret $R(T;\Vmax)= O(\Vmax\,  k^{1/3}\, T^{2/3}\, \log^{2/3} T)$.

results.notes: Mechanism is deterministic, truthful and normalized.

source.label: cor:weakly-truthful
source.quote: There exists a weakly truthful normalized mechanism for the adversarial MAB problem (against oblivious adversary) whose regret grows as $\bigo( (k\log k)^{1/3}\cdot T^{2/3}\cdot \vmax)$.

results.notes: Regret bound itself comes from Awerbuch-Kleinberg PSim analysis; new contribution is weak truthfulness. Payment computation efficiency not claimed.
